summary: Unequal routing after canary weight shift causes mixed model outputs for ongoing sessions
description: Customer BrightChat reports that after a planned canary weight adjustment at 2026-03-10T15:20Z, a subset of live chat sessions began receiving completions from a different model variant despite having been previously pinned. The customer observed content quality regressions and inconsistent conversation history in a small cohort (~0.9% of sessions).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start long-running chat session against tenant endpoint using SDK v1.12 with session affinity header set (X-Session-Affinity).
2) Simulate sustained traffic for ~10 minutes to warm caches and KV prefixes.
3) Trigger canary weight shift: increase canary from 2% to 25% via console rollout controller (time: 2026-03-10T15:20Z).
4) Observe session responses for 30 minutes after weight change and check model version reported in response metadata.
5) Confirm that affected sessions return model variant redwood/gpt-3.5-large-v1-canary while they were previously pinned to redwood/gpt-3.5-large-v1-stable.
observed_behavior: Pinned sessions intermittently lose version affinity immediately after the canary weight change and receive responses from the canary variant. This occurs without explicit unpinning in the control plane and affects only some SDK versions and edge nodes.
expected_behavior: Pinned sessions should maintain version affinity for their active lifetime or until an explicit unpin/promotion occurs. A global canary weight change should not rebind already-pinned sessions to the canary variant.

comments: 2026-03-10 - 15:35 - support@redwood - Hi BrightChat, we've acknowledged the report and started tracing edge logs. Can you confirm SDK version and whether you use sticky cookies or header affinity?
2026-03-10 - 15:42 - BrightChat-SRE - Confirm SDK v1.12. We set X-Session-Affinity header. Issue reproduces on roughly 1 in 100 sessions. Attached sample request IDs.
2026-03-10 - 16:10 - Daniel Morales - Initial hypothesis: race between routing cache eviction and async canary propagation. Assigning to infra for edge-proxy tracing.

2026-03-11 - 09:22 - infra@redwood - Found that edge-proxy versions <1.7 do not write affinity into persistent route cache on weight-change events; instead they rely on short TTLs. Upgrading edge nodes to 1.8 recommended as workaround.
2026-03-11 - 12:30 - BrightChat - After edge-proxy nodes were rolled to 1.8 in staging, we saw no reproductions. Can you advise production mitigation?
investigation_notes: Correlation: all affected sessions used SDK v1.12 and were served by a subset of edge nodes running edge-proxy 1.6/1.7.

Root cause hypothesis: canary-coordinator applies weight change async to route table; edge-proxy evicts short-lived route cache entries on weight-change and rewrites route without persisting session-affinity => subsequent requests routed to new variant.
Additional factor: certain SDK builds omit the explicit affinity cookie fallback, relying on header-only affinity which is lost when proxy rewrites requests.

Reproducible in internal test: reproduce with controlled weight change and mixed edge-proxy version fleet; failure occurs within <10 seconds post-change and affects ~0.7-1.2% of sessions in our test run.
Risk: ongoing rollouts that change weight quickly may impact long-lived session consistency for tenants using older SDKs or edge-proxy versions.
Related: linked to prior ticket SUP-8234 which described stale route-cache during gradual rollout but this incident is distinct due to async propagation timing and affinity write behavior.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: rolled edge-proxy fleet in us-east-1 to version 1.8 which persists session-affinity keys across route-table refreshes and increased route-cache write-through to reduce TTL evictions. Recommended customer-side workaround: upgrade SDK to >=1.13 which sets a persistent affinity cookie, or include explicit tenant-affinity header on every request.
post_action_items: 1) Infra: backport affinity-persistence patch to edge-proxy v1.7 (PR repo/edge-proxy#981) and schedule global rollout (owner: Daniel Morales).
2) Platform: change canary-coordinator to use synchronous affinity-preserving update path for weight changes when TTL-sensitive tenants are detected (owner: Priya Ramesh).
3) DX/Docs: update rollout runbook to add steps for 'affinity-safe' canary increases and a troubleshooting checklist for pinned session divergence (owner: Lauren Park).
4) Customer outreach: Send BrightChat an incident summary and recommend SDK upgrade and confirm mitigation (owner: CS Manager - Monica Lee).
